findings.reason: A front view of the repeated zero-eigenspace materially clarifies that the continuum consists of lines rather than oriented unit vectors: antipodal vectors are one Grassmann point. The original standalone tile renders the prose correctly but has no picture of this quotient identification. A useful expository figure is warranted under the expanded diagram scope.
findings.action: Added a final Remarks section with a planar TikZ schematic of sample minimizing lines and antipodal unit representatives.

correction: Appended explanatory Remarks and one native TikZ diagram; original title, Example, Facts, Proof, and full frontmatter are preserved.

diagram_math_checks.objects: E=span(e_1,e_2)=ker diag(0,0,2), drawn front-on with e_1,e_2 coordinate axes.
diagram_math_checks.check: For v=(a,b,c), Av=(0,0,2c); hence ker A is precisely the drawn coordinate plane. The transverse eigenvector has Ae_3=2e_3, so f([e_3])=2, unlike the minimizing zero values.
diagram_math_checks.local_basis: Example and proof step 1.1; direct multiplication of the given matrix.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Each solid/dashed straight sample through the origin represents a line in E, a point of Gr(1,3). The dashed circle represents the unit representatives in E at an arbitrary drawing scale.
diagram_math_checks.check: For any unit x in E, Ax=0 and x^T Ax=0; positive semidefiniteness makes this global minimum. Dashed lines are sample lines, not the complete family; the caption states this explicitly.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Opposite marked representatives x and -x on one emphasized line, with counterclockwise angle theta from e_1.
diagram_math_checks.check: The point coordinates are opposite and approximate 1.5(cos 35 degrees,sin 35 degrees); the highlighted diameter passes through the origin. The circle drawing scale 1.5 does not prescribe vector norm. O(1)={+1,-1} identifies the two unit representatives, so [x]=[-x].
diagram_math_checks.local_basis: Definition quotient by O(r), specialized to r=1; proof steps 1.1 and 2.1.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Half-open parameter range 0<=theta<pi in the Remarks.
diagram_math_checks.check: x(theta+pi)=-x(theta) gives the same line. Within [0,pi), equal lines require angle difference an integer multiple of pi and therefore equal parameters; no duplicated terminal endpoint is drawn or asserted. All lines of E are covered.
diagram_math_checks.local_basis: Proof step 2.1. The rigorous two-step proof is unchanged and independent of the figure.
